META.text: Meta fell about 7.9%, far more than the Nasdaq’s 2.1% decline, as Alphabet’s record cash burn and higher AI capex intensified concern that Meta’s own spending surge could pressure free cash flow ahead of its earnings; no new Meta-specific operating catalyst was confirmed.

NVDA.text: Nvidia gained about 2.0% despite a 2.1% Nasdaq decline, mostly because battered semiconductor shares rebounded sharply early in the week on renewed AI-demand optimism; Friday’s capex-driven chip selloff erased part of the gain, and no distinct Nvidia catalyst was confirmed.

AVGO.text: Broadcom gained about 3.0% as investors bought the prior week’s semiconductor dip after Morgan Stanley argued datacenter shortages still supported AI infrastructure demand; the move largely matched the chip rebound rather than reflecting new Broadcom news.

PLTR.text: Palantir fell about 7.1%, underperforming the Nasdaq, with no confirmed company-specific catalyst; the clearest explanation was a valuation-led selloff in high-multiple AI software ahead of its August 3 earnings, amplified by recent insider-sale optics.

SPCX.text: SpaceX fell about 7.2% as repeated Starship launch delays reinforced execution concerns while heavy short positioning and the approaching post-IPO lockup expiry kept selling pressure elevated; the move was company-specific rather than a broad-market decline.

MU.text: Micron gained about 8.5% after Morgan Stanley called the memory selloff a buying opportunity and projected sharply higher memory prices, then Tesla publicly thanked Micron for a significant chip allocation; Friday’s memory-sector pullback trimmed a much larger midweek gain.
